PullRequest.Title: fix(chat): release a remote chat model once its session is disposed
PullRequest.Body:
## Why

An Agent Host chat could reopen as read-only with no input box after its provider session was disposed, for example when a remote agent host connection was replaced. The host still considered the chat writable. Related to #318604.

## What changed

- `ChatService.trackRemoteSession` listens to the provided session's `onWillDispose` and calls a new `ChatModel.disableBackgroundKeepAlive()`.
- `ChatModel`'s background keep-alives (running request or pending input, and modified edits) now read an observable flag, so they release their self-reference once the session is gone.
- A model can now be released while its streamed turn still runs, so its tracking teardown removes the synthetic pending-request tracker it added. Otherwise a reopened idle session rejected sends with "Request already in progress". Disposing the tracker does not cancel the host turn.

Root cause: `loadRemoteSession` binds the model to `providedSession.isReadOnly` but never followed the session's lifetime. A model that kept itself alive outlived its session, and reopening reused it (`AgentHostChatSession.isReadOnly` is true once disposed) instead of loading a live session. #338211 fixed this for an in-progress turn only.

## Scope

All contributed session types loaded through `loadRemoteSession`. Holders other than the model itself, such as an open view, are unchanged. The chat view already reloads when its provider is replaced.

## Tradeoffs

A disposed session's model no longer stays alive in the background for a pending question or unreviewed edits. That state could not be acted on anyway, since the session behind it is gone. The next open reloads it from the host.

## Blast Radius

Only models whose provided session is disposed while the model lives. Local chats and live remote sessions keep their keep-alives.

## Verification

- Two new unit tests, each committed failing before its fix: reopening after disposal loads a live, writable model; and a session disposed mid-turn does not block sends after reopening.
- `./scripts/test.sh --runGlob "**/contrib/chat/test/**/*.test.js"`: 19815 passing, 1 failing (`ChatListWidget` full-refresh test, which also fails on the base commit).
- `pnpm run typecheck-client` and `pnpm run oxlint` on the changed files: passed.
- Agents window with a local standalone agent host: a chat kept alive by pending input, the host removed and re-added, then the chat reopened. Disposal path: `RemoteAgentHostContribution._reconcileConnections` → `ConnectionState.dispose` → `AgentHostSessionHandler.dispose` → `AgentHostChatSession.dispose`. [Before](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/blob/17e91b4e4f39310d6297ac952d14419f8631792b/vscode/agent-host-disposed-session/before.png): input hidden, model read-only. [After](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/blob/17e91b4e4f39310d6297ac952d14419f8631792b/vscode/agent-host-disposed-session/after.png): fresh load with the input present, and [a follow-up message got a reply](https://github.com/ulugbekna/screenshots/blob/17e91b4e4f39310d6297ac952d14419f8631792b/vscode/agent-host-disposed-session/after-send.png). Steps and state readouts are in a comment below.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The provider-wide disposal loop, observable self-reference release, reference-count teardown, singleton persistence call, global Sequencer and unconditional object-to-string conversion were traced directly. The effective count is the number of models with no remaining external holders that were kept alive by edits/input, not all history entries. Duration and typical counts are unmeasured; database writes are coalesced, so the finding concerns CPU/allocation rather than N disk writes.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and temporary strings for full chat-metadata index serialization.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N otherwise-unowned background models released by one provider disposal and B bytes of persisted index metadata, the new path performs N complete serializations, O(N*B), instead of a single O(B) group flush. N excludes models still held by open views; B includes the whole index, not just the disposed provider's models. Persistent database writes remain coalesced by storage key.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Additional main-thread serialization and allocation can stall UI responsiveness during provider replacement and increase GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: These closed models remained rooted by their background self-references after provider disposal, so this event did not run their metadata-disposal jobs. Ordinary saveState persisted live external models together through storeSessionsMetadataOnly(liveNonLocalChats), with one index flush for that batch. Releasing invalid models is necessary, but the newly reached per-model persistence duplicates the collection-wide serialization.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Provider removal or replacement now releases every otherwise-unowned background model, routing each independently through singleton metadata persistence. That performs a full chat-index serialization for every released model rather than persisting the group once.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: chatServiceImpl.ts:1265 newly disables both model self-references on providedSession.onWillDispose. For N closed models still kept alive by Modified edits, AgentHostSessionHandler.dispose's existing loop now causes N last-reference releases, whereas those models previously remained alive. Each release invokes willDisposeModel at chatServiceImpl.ts:395-399 with storeSessionsMetadataOnly([model]), newly scheduling N separate full-index serializations for one provider replacement.
Findings.Title: Batch metadata persistence when releasing background sessions
Findings.Impact: Replacing or removing an agent host after accumulating multiple closed chats with unreviewed edits or pending input now serializes the entire history index repeatedly during teardown. With a large persisted index, this adds UI-thread CPU and temporary strings, delaying UI responsiveness and creating GC pressure even though the actual database write is coalesced.
Findings.Evidence: RemoteAgentHostContribution._reconcileConnections (remoteAgentHostChatContribution.ts:283-288) disposes and recreates contribution state on clientId/name replacement. AgentHostSessionHandler.dispose (9250-9255) disposes all active provider sessions. The new listener clears background references via chatModel.ts:3370-3374 and 3393-3397. ChatModelStore.destroyReferencedObject (190-217) invokes the disposal delegate for each last-reference release; chatServiceImpl.ts:395-399 calls storeSessionsMetadataOnly([model]). chatSessionStore.ts:214-217 serializes these jobs through one Sequencer and flushes the complete index after each singleton update; flushIndex:422-426 passes the index object to storageService.store. Storage.set (base/parts/storage/common/storage.ts:264-284) stringifies the entire object before equality checking. The database layer coalesces pendingInserts by key and throttles flushes, but cannot coalesce these preceding serializations. Existing saveState (chatServiceImpl.ts:475-488) demonstrates group persistence using the array API.
Findings.Recommendation: Keep the new lifetime release, but coalesce simultaneous model-disposal metadata updates into the existing array-based storeSessionsMetadataOnly API and flush the index once. Preserve each model's disposal wait until its metadata has been captured.

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The modified-edits keep-alive retained a strong ChatModel reference without following its provider session lifetime. Once the provider was disposed, Modified entries could remain indefinitely, retaining each closed model's requests, response contents and editing resources; retained bytes grew with distinct affected sessions and their histories/edits.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Strongly evidenced indefinite retention of closed remote chat models after provider replacement or removal when unreviewed edits remain, accumulating memory across affected sessions.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Disposal of the bound remote session disables both background self-reference conditions. Models with no other holders now reach reference-counted teardown and release conversation and editing resources instead of remaining rooted by unreviewed edits or pending input.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: The base keep-alive autorun computed hasModified solely from session.entries and entry.state (base line 3385), acquiring a ChatService reference whenever any edit remained Modified. AgentHostSessionHandler.dispose (9250-9255) disposes every active provider session; AgentHostChatSession.dispose (1023-1037) completes progress but does not accept/reject modified edits. ChatModelStore only destroys a model after its reference count reaches zero (190-217), so closing the view leaves the self-reference rooting the full ChatModel, conversation responses and editing session indefinitely after the provider is gone. The PR adds the provider onWillDispose listener at chatServiceImpl.ts:1265 and gates the modified-edits autorun with a mutable observable at chatModel.ts:3393; setting it clears the self-reference. ChatModel.dispose:3928-3942 then disposes responses and clears heavy fields. Blame of the original hasModified expression identifies 82d482408fccbb36addd2e56120b517d1bdbccd6, origin common/chatModel.ts. The added reopen test independently demonstrates formerly unreleasable in-progress models now reaching disposal, though edit retention is established statically.

Scenarios.Scenario: Remove or replace an agent host with closed background chats retained by pending input or unreviewed edits.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The connection reconciliation event synchronously disposes the old handler and provider sessions. The new observable flag releases model self-references. Actual model destruction waits for metadata capture/persistence scheduling; the metadata jobs serialize the complete index in a chain of microtasks on the UI thread. Database flushes are delayed and are not awaited by storageService.store.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist each disposed model's metadata through a singleton batch and stringify the complete chat index.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: N metadata updates and N full-index object-to-string conversions, O(N*B), for newly releasable models. Not one serialization per history row.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The affected models remained self-retained after provider disposal and did not schedule these teardown jobs. Normal saveState used group updates for live external models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: UI-thread serialization and allocation occur during the ensuing teardown microtask chain; the final model disposal awaits its metadata job.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Flush coalesced pending storage insertions to the backing database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Multiple index updates are coalesced by storage key into delayed database flushes; not N mandatory database operations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Affected retained models had no disposal-triggered update; periodic grouped saves and their database flushes already existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Database updateItems is off the synchronous reconciliation path and does not block model teardown through storageService.store.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Release existing session/chat subscriptions and send unsubscribe notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one unsubscribe per unique subscription whose final owner releases; shared sibling-chat subscriptions survive. Handler disposal already releases its subscription maps.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same handler teardown already disposed provider sessions and subscription references. The PR changes model lifetime, not the handler's subscription loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Notifications do not wait for a remote response. New synthetic tracker disposal does not cancel the host turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N distinct loaded models for that provider whose last external holder is gone and whose self-reference was keeping them alive; exclude open-view models and already-disposable idle models. B is the byte size of the full persisted chat-metadata index. Editing cleanup also scales with entries whose reference counts reach zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Provider disposal loops synchronously over sessions. Model teardown begins independently, but metadata jobs use one global ChatSessionStore Sequencer, not N concurrent database writes. Each singleton job still performs a complete serialization. Entry disposal is reference-counted, and resources shared with surviving sessions remain alive.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The provider-session cache already evicts disposed sessions; the PR additionally permits model-cache eviction after the final holder release. Index data and serialized storage values are cached, but Storage.set stringifies objects before comparing cached values. Pending database inserts overwrite the same index key and are throttled, coalescing writes but not serialization.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: traced the provider-wide loop, mutable flag, reference-count destruction, singleton persistence calls, global sequencing, serialization-before-deduplication and deferred database batching.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of concurrently retained chats, index byte size and milliseconds of UI disruption are unmeasured. Provider replacement is less frequent than streaming. These magnitude uncertainties justify low severity, while the repeated full-index serialization mechanism is established.
Scenarios.Verdict: One low-severity missing-coalescing finding submitted for newly multiplied full-index serializations. The lifetime change also fixes indefinite model retention; that separate regression-fix signal was submitted with blame provenance.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reopen a contributed remote chat after its disposed model has lost all holders.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A cache miss must resolve the provider, obtain session content, hydrate backend session/chat state, build history and publish the restored model before the chat can use it. Historical replay is cooperatively scheduled with existing 25 ms slices. Default-agent initialization is launched asynchronously rather than awaited before returning the model.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve contributed-session content through its current provider after model-cache eviction.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provideChatSessionContent call per cold distinct resource, not per history turn or consumer; zero for warm model hits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: This cold-load path already existed; for the specific previously stuck model, reopening incorrectly returned the retained model without loading the current provider. The PR intentionally invalidates that unusable cache entry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session content must be returned before model restoration and publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Subscribe to and hydrate backend session/chat snapshots, including existing active subagent enrichment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold subscription acquisition serves S backend-session channels plus C chat channels and U deduplicated active/legacy child channels. Already-held channels are reused, and settled subagent histories do not eagerly hydrate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cold-load subscription grouping and enrichment behavior; no new per-turn or per-file fan-out is added. Previously stuck warm models skipped cold loading entirely.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Session then chat hydration, and active child enrichment, are awaited before content is returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover and register backend session identities.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One shared in-flight listSessions request per handler when required identities are unknown; no request for advertised or provisional identities.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped identity-discovery fallback existed for cold loads.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Unknown identity resolution is awaited before normal hydration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One model load per distinct chat resource, shared among concurrent consumers. For agent-host chats, S distinct backend sessions, C unique chat channels, and U unique active/legacy subagent channels requiring restoration; settled child histories are deferred. History CPU/allocation scales with loaded turns and response parts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Same-resource consumers share a load; cancelled predecessor loads are awaited before retry. Session hydration precedes chat hydration within a load. Different resources can load concurrently without a newly added global limiter. Active child restoration uses Promise.all after child-URI deduplication; existing cooperative replay yields between work slices.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live model hits bypass provider loading. In-flight loads and provider resolutions are coalesced per resource. Provider-session caches evict on disposal. Backend session subscriptions are shared by backend session URI and chat subscriptions by channel URI. Subagent loads deduplicate promises by child URI, including empty outcomes within that enrichment pass. Unknown backend identities share one in-flight listSessions refresh per handler. Failed subscription entries are evicted for retry; cancelled loads settle before replacement attempts.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cache invalidation, per-resource coalescing and agent-host subscription grouping; arbitrary contributed provider internals remain outside the bounded investigation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: History length, active child count, provider-specific transport/pagination and snapshot latency vary. Static review does not measure reload time or all third-party provider implementations.
Scenarios.Verdict: Fresh hydration after an unusable provider session is intentional and necessary. No independently reportable reload fan-out or eager-history regression was found.

Scenarios.Scenario: Dispose a provider mid-stream, then reopen the idle chat and send a follow-up request.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Old model teardown removes only the synthetic tracker owned by that model. Reopening waits for normal restoration; sending waits for pending remote history mutations and existing request arbitration, then invokes the agent and dispatches the new turn. Synthetic disposal itself waits for no network response.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Invoke the provider and dispatch ChatTurnStarted to the agent host.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One normal turn-start dispatch per accepted follow-up; no extra request caused by synthetic cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Normal follow-up dispatch was the same whenever no stale tracker blocked it. The added cleanup restores that existing behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The agent invocation drives normal response progress. Sending is no longer rejected solely by the stale synthetic pending tracker.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Distinguish local synthetic-token disposal from the existing explicit remote interruption path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero host interruption/tool-cancellation calls from disposing this synthetic tracker; existing explicit cancellation can invoke one interruption callback.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Synthetic trackers were disposed on normal completion and explicit steering as before, but not on this newly possible mid-turn model teardown.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Tracker cleanup is local and does not await or cancel the host's active turn.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: At most one current pending-request map entry and one remembered synthetic tracker per live model; subsequent synthetic trackers replace the remembered pointer. Streaming processes only progress appended since lastProgressLength. Each follow-up submission produces its normal agent invocation/turn dispatch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Request arbitration and queues remain per session. Other sessions may progress independently. Synthetic disposal uses CancellationTokenSource.dispose, not cancel, and synthetic requestId is undefined, so this cleanup does not dispatch tool cancellation or interrupt RPCs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Synthetic membership is held in a WeakSet. The map cleanup checks tracker identity so a replacement or real request is not removed. A disposed model's tracker no longer remains in the pending map. Model/content cache behavior matches the preceding scenario.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inspected CancellableRequest.dispose, synthetic construction arguments, WeakSet ownership, identity guard, streaming processing and follow-up dispatch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cancellation UI/provider latency varies, but no new expensive call is introduced by the changed tracker cleanup.
Scenarios.Verdict: Cleanup is bounded and removes stale retained state without cancelling remote work. No new performance regression found in tracker lifetime or streaming frequency.

Scenarios.Scenario: Create and use live local chats, quick chat, or models whose background keep-alive was disabled at construction.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: ChatModel construction adds a small observable and installs bounded keep-alive autoruns. The request autorun still reads progress/input state when disabled; the edit autorun short-circuits before scanning entries. Existing model restoration, editing-session creation and asynchronous agent activation remain in their prior places.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read or persist local chat data through the existing session store.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing local restore reads and persistence writes retain their prior per-session/grouping behavior; zero new filesystem operations from the observable flag or keep-alive gate.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same local restore/persistence calls and scheduling.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold local restore still waits for stored session data. The PR does not move local storage work onto a new path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request existing extension-agent activation when applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing initializeSession may request default-agent activation once for each constructed model; there is no new activation call in the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization is launched asynchronously, outside the model-return critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One new boolean observable per model, one request keep-alive autorun for Chat-location models, and an edit keep-alive autorun per startEditingSession call. Edit-state scanning is unchanged for enabled models and skipped for disabled models. Repeated startEditingSession observer setup is otherwise pre-existing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable updates run synchronously. Existing file persistence uses the ChatSessionStore Sequencer; initialization is started without awaiting it on model creation. No changed subprocess creation, limiter or IPC fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The disable flag is one-way and equality-based, not a growing map or history. Existing response pending-confirmation derivations are shared within the observable graph. Local model/store caches and session serialization policy are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded added state, short-circuiting edit reads and unchanged boundary placement.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Small additional observer costs are unmeasured. No concrete scaling or expensive-boundary multiplication was established for initially disabled models.
Scenarios.Verdict: No high-confidence performance regression found in the bounded observable/autorun changes or live/local behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance-review pass over all three changed files and every diff page. Submitted one low-severity finding for full-index serialization multiplied by newly enabled bulk background-model teardown, accounting for globally sequenced metadata jobs and coalesced database writes. Recorded a concrete retained-model memory regression fix with original-line blame provenance. Investigated cache invalidation, provider replacement, fresh loading, shared subscriptions/subagent restoration, synthetic cancellation ownership and initially disabled/live/local models. Static read-only review; no profiling or repository execution.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
